overview.title: Welcome to Laâyoune — Where the Desert Meets the Atlantic
overview.p1: Laâyoune is the largest city and economic heart of the Moroccan Sahara. Situated on the dry bed of the Saguia el-Hamra river and just 25 kilometers from the Atlantic shore, it bridges modern urban development with centuries-old nomadic customs.
overview.p2: From traditional three-round Sahrawi tea ceremonies to fresh seafood catches at the port of El Marsa and peaceful ocean sunsets at Foum El Oued beach, Laâyoune offers an authentic southern desert experience.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Laâyoune
places.subtitle: Monuments, Atlantic beaches, desert oases, and vibrant local markets.

jemaa.title: Place du Méchouar
jemaa.desc: The historic and ceremonial heart of Laâyoune, framed by landscaped walkways, shaded trees, and Saharan architectural touches. Ideal for an evening stroll, people-watching, and experiencing local city life.

majorelle.title: Foum El Oued Beach
majorelle.desc: A wide stretch of golden sand along the Atlantic coast just outside Laâyoune. Popular for brisk walks beside the surf, refreshing ocean air, and wide-open sunsets over the water.

bahia.title: El Marsa Port
bahia.desc: A major maritime hub in southern Morocco lively with fishing vessels, working quays, and crisp Atlantic light. It highlights Laâyoune's strong connection to the ocean and coastal trade.

ben_youssef.title: Saguia El Hamra
ben_youssef.desc: An iconic valley cutting through arid terrain and lending its name to the region. It creates a striking contrast between mineral expanses, palm groves, and the region's natural identity.

saadian.title: Souk Soune
saadian.desc: A lively traditional market filled with Saharan textiles, handicrafts, spices, and everyday goods. A great place to discover local craftsmanship and interact with vendors.

elbadi.title: Spanish Quarter
elbadi.desc: A district shaped by facades, small squares, and architectural lines rooted in the past, woven into Laâyoune's urban fabric. A calm walk to trace how the city's architecture evolved.

jardin_menara.title: Moulay Abdellah Mosque
jardin_menara.desc: A major mosque in Laâyoune recognizable by its monumental scale and presence within the city. It serves both as a prominent landmark and a central place of prayer.

dar_el_bacha.title: Lemsid Dunes
dar_el_bacha.desc: Striking sand dunes north of Laâyoune shaped by Saharan winds. Ideal for watching shifting desert light, walking along the ridges, and enjoying quiet open spaces.

koutoubia.title: Place Oulad Tedrarag
koutoubia.desc: Lush palm park providing cool shade and evening family promenades.

place_oulad_tedrarag.title: Oulad Tedrarag Square
place_oulad_tedrarag.desc: A lively public square that reflects everyday life in Laâyoune. A familiar meeting and passing spot valued for its friendly neighborhood atmosphere.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan to discover the city landmarks, the port, and the surrounding desert.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Stroll around Place Mechouar, admiring the Sahrawi architectural motifs and broad palm-lined boulevards.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Browse traditional silver jewelry, camel-leather goods, and colorful melhfa fabrics in local markets.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Experience local tea hospitality (Atay) served in three distinct rounds in a relaxed city café.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Head west to the port town of El Marsa to observe fishing boats returning with the daily Atlantic catch.
detailed_itinerary.day2_a: Afternoon — Foum El Oued Ocean Relax
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Enjoy lunch with freshly grilled fish, then unwind along the wide sandy beach of Foum El Oued.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Watch the sunset as the golden desert dunes merge directly into the ocean shore.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Explore the palm groves and dry river bed landscapes north-east of Laâyoune.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Take a short camel trek across the golden dunes surrounding the city limits.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Enjoy camel meat tagine or fresh grilled sea bass in one of Laâyoune's authentic local restaurants.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.desc: Yellow petit taxis are plentiful and economical within the city. Grand taxis run frequently to El Marsa and Foum El Oued beach.

bargain.title: Weather & Climate
bargain.desc: Enjoyable sunny desert climate year-round with mild Atlantic ocean breezes. Evening temperatures can drop noticeably in winter.

water.title: Sahrawi Etiquette
water.desc: Hospitality is deep-rooted. Accepting tea when offered is customary. Respect local social norms and ask before photographing people.

agafay.desc: UNESCO biosphere reserve lagoon for birdwatching and sand dunes.

ouzoud.title: Smara Oasis Town
ouzoud.desc: Historic spiritual desert city inland along the Saguia el-Hamra.

essaouira.title: Boujdour Coast Drive
essaouira.desc: Scenic coastal road driving south with dramatic ocean cliffs.

q1.question: Is Laâyoune easy to reach?
q1.answer: Yes, Hassan I Airport (EUN) offers regular direct domestic flights from Casablanca and Agadir, as well as international connections. The N1 coastal highway connects it smoothly by road.

q2.question: How far is the beach from the city?
q2.answer: Foum El Oued beach and the port of El Marsa are located about 20 to 25 kilometers west of the city center, reachable in 20 minutes by taxi or car.

q3.question: How many days should I spend in Laâyoune?
q3.answer: 2 to 3 days allow you to explore the city squares, enjoy fresh seafood at the port, relax on Foum El Oued beach, and take a dune excursion.

q4.question: What is the best month to visit Laâyoune?
q4.answer: From October to April, the climate is pleasantly warm and sunny, avoiding the intense heat of peak summer.

place_mechouar.title: Méchouar Square (Place du Méchouar)
place_mechouar.p1: Méchouar Square is one of the defining open spaces of central Laâyoune, offering wide sightlines, landscaped walkways and a welcoming civic atmosphere that anchors nearby avenues.
place_mechouar.p2: Strolling around the square in the late afternoon lets you observe everyday city rhythm, meet locals and connect easily toward adjacent neighbourhoods and markets.
place_mechouar.tip: Best visited around sunset when temperatures soften and the square feels most lively.

moulay_abdellah.title: Moulay Abdellah Mosque
moulay_abdellah.p1: Rising prominently within Laâyoune, Moulay Abdellah Mosque stands out for its generous proportions, geometric motifs and strong visual presence along the city skyline.
moulay_abdellah.p2: Even from the outside, its courtyards, facade details and surrounding open space make it an essential architectural landmark for understanding contemporary religious building in the south.
moulay_abdellah.tip: Dress respectfully around the mosque and avoid blocking entrances during prayer times.

spanish_quarter.p1: The Spanish Quarter preserves low-rise blocks, arcaded walkways and small plazas that reflect an earlier chapter of Laâyoune's urban planning woven into the modern city.
spanish_quarter.p2: Walking through its streets reveals subtle contrasts between older facades, shaded corners and active local shops that give the district its distinctive character.
spanish_quarter.tip: Explore on foot at an unhurried pace to notice architectural details on upper facades.

souk_soune.title: Souk Soune
souk_soune.p1: Souk Soune is a vibrant hub of local commerce where visitors encounter traditional Saharan textiles, handcrafted goods, spices, tea supplies and everyday household items.
souk_soune.p2: Moving between stalls offers an authentic look at regional tastes and textures, making it a rewarding stop for souvenirs, fabrics and friendly exchanges with merchants.
souk_soune.tip: Go in the morning or early evening when stalls are active and carry small cash bills.

saguia_el_hamra.title: Saguia El Hamra Valley
saguia_el_hamra.p1: Saguia El Hamra gives its name to the region and traces a striking natural corridor of palm groves, dry channels and arid banks right beside Laâyoune.
saguia_el_hamra.p2: The contrast between clusters of greenery, ochre earth and wide skies creates a memorable sense of place that connects the city directly to its southern environment.
saguia_el_hamra.tip: Bring sun protection and a camera for wide landscape views in clear daylight.

el_marsa_port.p1: Located on the coast west of the city centre, El Marsa Port is a major maritime anchor driven by fishing boats, marine activity and fresh Atlantic catches.
el_marsa_port.p2: Watching boats, harbour infrastructure and ocean swells gives clear insight into how coastal trade and fisheries shape life across the region.
el_marsa_port.tip: Stay clear of active quays and heavy loading gear, and check local access rules.

foum_el_oued.p1: Just a short drive from Laâyoune, Foum El Oued opens onto a broad Atlantic shoreline where long stretches of sand meet rolling waves and crisp coastal air.
foum_el_oued.p2: Visitors come to walk along the tide line, unwind beside the ocean and take in wide sunsets where desert light meets the Atlantic.
foum_el_oued.tip: Atlantic currents and waves can be strong — stay mindful of sea conditions.
